GCD(3, 12) = 3, so divide top and bottom by 3 to get 1/4. Check for improper form: 1/4 is proper (top < bottom), so it's already in final form — no mixed number needed.

questions.prompt: Where does one pair of brackets go to make this true?  {5/2} × {3/5} - {2/5} + {1/2} = 1
questions.steps: Without brackets the multiplication goes first and you get 3/2 - 2/5 + 1/2, which is not 1. Group the subtraction instead: 3/5 - 2/5 = 1/5, then 5/2 × 1/5 = 1/2, and 1/2 + 1/2 = 1.
questions.tip: Try each one. Brackets force whatever is inside them to happen first, so ask which grouping would change the answer to the one you want.

questions.prompt: A school fair sells {4_1/2} trays of veggie pizza, {5_2/3} trays of pepperoni and {3_3/4} trays of cheese. How many trays were sold altogether?
questions.steps: Add all three: 9/2 + 17/3 + 15/4. The LCM of 2, 3 and 4 is 12, so that is 54/12 + 68/12 + 45/12 = 167/12. Check for reducing: GCD(167, 12) = 1, so 167/12 is already in simplest form. Check for improper form: 167/12 is improper (top ≥ bottom), so convert it to the mixed number 13 11/12.

questions.steps: Half a box is 8 × 1/2 = 4 balls and a whole box is 8. Add the three amounts: 4 + 8 + 3 = 15 balls.

questions.prompt: Leah ate {1/3} of a pie and Mira ate {1/4} of the same pie. The next day Nina ate {3/5} of what was still left. What fraction of the pie was never eaten?
questions.steps: Day one: 1/3 + 1/4 = 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12 eaten, leaving 5/12. Nina ate 3/5 × 5/12 = 3/12 of the whole pie. What is left is 5/12 - 3/12 = 2/12. Reduce first: your raw fraction never eaten is 2/12. GCD(2, 12) = 2, so divide top and bottom by 2 to get 1/6. Check for improper form: 1/6 is proper (top < bottom), so it's already in final form — no mixed number needed.

questions.prompt: A ball bounces back to {2/3} of the height it fell from, every time. It is dropped from 81 cm. How high is the 4th bounce, in cm?
questions.steps: Each bounce multiplies the height by 2/3, so after four bounces it is 81 × (2/3)⁴ = 81 × 16/81. The exponent is worked out before the multiplying, and then the 81s cancel. Check for reducing: GCD(16, 1) = 1, so 16/1 is already in simplest form. It actually simplifies all the way down to a whole number.
